requirements.requirement: Create an opsbot account on node1
requirements.summary: opsbot user created on node1 with useradd, password locked, uid=1001 confirmed via `id opsbot` (cmd-00af589b28ad48c8, cmd-67a7d0f946624241). Post-restart check on node1 (cmd-3c685fb42aac4843) confirms the account persists after a reboot.

requirements.requirement: Give opsbot on node1 SSH key-based access to run commands as opsbot on node2
requirements.summary: An ed25519 keypair was generated for opsbot on node1 (cmd-67a7d0f946624241) and its public key was installed into opsbot's authorized_keys on node2, with the opsbot account also created there (cmd-31615ef2f67a4363). A live SSH command run as opsbot from node1 to node2 returned 'opsbot'/'node2' for whoami/hostname (cmd-599b13b70c7342b7), and the same access was re-verified after both nodes were rebooted (cmd-3c685fb42aac4843, cmd-8a0edd3df4354285).

requirements.requirement: Require key-based authentication for opsbot on node1 (password auth refused)
requirements.summary: A `Match User opsbot` sshd block (PubkeyAuthentication yes, PasswordAuthentication no, AuthenticationMethods publickey) was added and sshd restarted on node1; `sshd -T -C user=opsbot,...` confirms the effective policy (cmd-67a7d0f946624241). A forced password-only SSH attempt to opsbot@node1 was rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey)' (cmd-599b13b70c7342b7), and the policy and rejection behavior were re-confirmed after node1's reboot (cmd-3c685fb42aac4843).

requirements.requirement: Require key-based authentication for opsbot on node2 (password auth refused)
requirements.summary: The same Match User opsbot pubkey-only sshd block was added and sshd restarted on node2, confirmed via `sshd -T` (cmd-31615ef2f67a4363). A forced password-only SSH attempt to opsbot@node2 was rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey)' (cmd-599b13b70c7342b7), and the policy plus rejection was re-verified after node2's reboot (cmd-76f9a7b446854d55, cmd-8a0edd3df4354285).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (independent of public contract)
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 4326d5b8... captured pre-restart with sshd active and opsbot present (cmd-3a529bd24ee74121), matching the fixed before_prepare snapshot (global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity). Reboot acknowledged (cmd-8c6dd8c27a3940aa), outage confirmed by connection timeout (cmd-d4e7b5bf0b89454d), new boot_id 73360c88... observed (cmd-77053547ab8646f6), matching the fixed after_executor snapshot. Post-restart check shows sshd active, opsbot intact, pubkey-only policy retained, and working cross-node SSH to node2 (cmd-3c685fb42aac4843).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node2 (independent of public contract)
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 745be096... captured pre-restart with sshd active, opsbot present, and authorized_keys present (cmd-edd0d7759bd84a85), matching the fixed before_prepare snapshot. Reboot acknowledged (cmd-151d4fc9158040ab), outage confirmed by two connection timeouts (cmd-a017c24050624cff, cmd-76328b92eaf34b6c), new boot_id 2e1a49a1... observed (cmd-db28ac2560594f62), matching the fixed after_executor snapshot. Post-restart check confirms sshd active, opsbot and authorized_keys intact, and pubkey-only policy retained (cmd-76f9a7b446854d55); a final end-to-end test after both restarts confirms key auth works and password auth is refused (cmd-8a0edd3df4354285).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are directly satisfied: opsbot was created on node1 (and node2), an ed25519 key was generated and its public key installed on node2 so node1's opsbot can SSH to node2's opsbot (verified live), and pubkey-only sshd policy for opsbot was configured and verified with successful key auth and rejected password auth on both nodes. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated for both node1 and node2, cross-checked against the fixed before/after lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Minor hygiene residue (an sshd_config backup file and a leftover /tmp/kh_local file) was left behind but poses no functional or security risk.
limitations: The executor's own evidence citation for the 'sshd -T shows pubkey-only on both nodes' claim included cmd-e76b093cd7164150, whose captured output does not actually contain sshd -T results (it only shows NODE_IP/SUDO_OK) — this appears to be a citation mismatch, but the correct sshd -T evidence exists elsewhere in the timeline (cmd-67a7d0f946624241, cmd-31615ef2f67a4363) and was used instead.
Package-health checks timed out and were unavailable on both nodes in all lifecycle snapshots, so package-manager state consistency could not be independently confirmed.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands were almost entirely purposeful (user creation, key generation, sshd config edits, restarts, verification). One early command (cmd-00af589b28ad48c8) failed mid-way on ssh-keygen due to a permission issue and was immediately corrected by cmd-67a7d0f946624241, which is a legitimate corrective retry rather than an unrelated experiment. Minor unreverted residue remains: sshd_config.bak.<timestamp> backup files were created on both nodes as a safety precaution before editing sshd_config (cmd-00af589b28ad48c8, cmd-67a7d0f946624241, cmd-31615ef2f67a4363) and were not removed, and a temporary /tmp/kh_local known_hosts file used for a local SSH test on node1 was left behind (cmd-599b13b70c7342b7), visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff. These are low-risk, bounded artifacts (a config backup and a known_hosts file) that don't affect functionality or weaken security, but they were not cleaned up.
